# Claim bot explains claiming after an unrecognized comment

## Context

The operator requested this bounded feature on 16 Nov 2026 after #21180's comment6929666240 received no reply. The bot ran successfully ([run43958790849](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/43958790849)); its text matcher returned no claim/withdrawal. An unfamiliar contributor therefore receives no claiming instructions.

Design authority: the operator approved one explanatory hint per contributor per unclaimed ticket, without suppressing a later `/claim`.

## The Problem

`isClaim()` intentionally recognizes explicit claim phrases; widening it would assign ambiguous offers. The fallback should explain the command without creating ownership or promising availability/payment.

## The Architectural Reality

At dev `ba5a511879`, `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs` owns pure reply/holder decisions and distinct bot receipts. `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` drops unrecognized `issue_comment` events before reading live holder state. `holders()` accounts for prior claims and resolving PRs, but excludes the current claimant; guidance needs a neutral observer and current evaluation time. Existing unit/workflow-replay specs live under `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/`.

## The Fix

Add the pure guidance decision in sibling `buildScripts/util/claimGuidance.mjs`, importing the existing reply module's holder and identity rules, and invoke it from the existing workflow for unrecognized outside comments on open curated issues. Reuse complete holder reads; recheck live state before posting. Deduplicate guidance by numeric contributor ID and issue with a distinct marker accepted only from the workflow bot. Retain the current claim and withdrawal paths.

Suggested text: “If you'd like to work on this issue, comment `/claim`. The bot will check availability and confirm the result. See the contributing guide.” Link the repository's `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guidance decision | operator request | a hint only for an open curated issue with no assignee, live claim or resolving PR; outside human only | unknown/incomplete state emits no hint | JSDoc | pure cases |
| Guidance receipt | existing trusted bot receipts | one hint per numeric account per issue; separate from claim receipts | copied/untrusted marker grants no authority | JSDoc | rename/replay/forgery cases |
| Workflow issue-comment branch | current claim workflow | complete reads and fresh pre-post eligibility; never assign for a hint | failed reads fail without a write | workflow comment | actual callback replay |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: An unrecognized outside comment on an open unclaimed `good first issue` or `help wanted` issue gets a brief `/claim` explanation linking `CONTRIBUTING.md`; it makes no assignment or availability/payment promise.
- [ ] AC-2: At most one hint is emitted per contributor ID and issue across repeated comments/replays and login changes; different contributors remain independent. Only a trusted workflow-bot hint receipt suppresses another hint.
- [ ] AC-3: A later valid `/claim` still reaches normal standing/holder checks and assignment. A hint is neither an earlier claim nor an accepted/refused claim receipt.
- [ ] AC-4: No hint for PR comments, team/bot authors, closed/uncurated issues, recognized claims/withdrawals, any assignee, live claims or resolving PRs (including the commenter's own). A claim arriving after the triggering comment also blocks the hint.
- [ ] AC-5: Workflow replay verifies current state and dedup before posting; unavailable/incomplete reads and a newly appearing holder produce no hint. Focused owning specs and repository-required checks pass.

## Post-Merge Validation

Observe the first genuine eligible outside comment after deployment and retain its hint plus subsequent `/claim` result when one arrives. No historical-comment backfill or artificial contributor account is required.

## Out of Scope

Changing claim recognition/standing/withdrawal policy, LLM classification, payment negotiation, historical replies, contributor guide rewrite (the existing guide is linked), and shared service settings.

## Avoided Traps

- Treating an unknown comment as a claim or reusing its receipt marker.
- Checking only assignees, excluding the commenter's own holder, or evaluating queued hints at the old event time.
- Repeated procedural replies to the same contributor or letting a hint suppress a later `/claim`.
